To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) ecological resilience is the ability of an ecological system to maintain a given set of ecological properties and functions in the face of disturbance, and 2) the ability of an ecosystem to absorb disturbance is a function of both its resistance to disturbance (i.e., its ability to maintain its structure, function, and processes in the face of the disturbance) and its recovery rate after disturbance (i.e. its ability to return to its pre-disturbance structure, function, or processes).

the resilience of ecosystems can be effectively managed if: 1) the resilience concept and the underlying theory is understood; 2) the ecological system is well characterized, with a clear understanding of the drivers of change; 3) a range of resilience metrics is used; and 4) the management strategy is designed to achieve the desired resilience.
